newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-SOUTH AFRICA BACKS IDEA OF WORLD TEST CHAMPIONSHIP.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SOUTH AFRICA BACKS IDEA OF WORLD TEST CHAMPIONSHIP.

text.p: The United Cricket Board of South Africa (UCBSA) backed on Monday a proposal to form a world test championship.
At a news conference, UCBSA managing director Ali Bacher said his board would back a proposal by Matthew Engel, the editor of Wisden, to create a league table for the test playing nations.
Bacher said: "Engel's proposal is well thought out and presented and we will be giving it our backing at the next International Cricket Council (ICC) meeting in June 1997."

Engel's blueprint envisages each test nation playing each of the others over a four-year cycle. The series may be as many as five tests or as few as one with two points allocated to the winner, one each for a draw and no points for a series defeat.

Bacher said: "I think the time is ripe to take a fresh look at the way test matches are organised and this seems to be a good recipe. I have studied Engel's proposal and over the next four years it would only require South Africa to add a home test aginst Zimbabwe to our existing commitments."
Bacher said that he had spoken to Engel on the telephone and was due to meet him in London on December 4.

In other developments, Bacher announced that South Africa would play three home tests against Pakistan and two against Sri Lanka in February and March 1998. The three teams will them play a triangular one-day international series.
